BiblicalUsage: Chared is trembling, fearful and reverential at once, and it is the trembling God looks for. Every one that trembled at the words of the God of Israel assembled to Ezra, God says He will look to him that is poor and of a contrite spirit and trembleth at His word, and the same promise is given to those who tremble at His word when their brethren cast them out. Eli sat by the wayside with his heart trembling for the ark of God.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this trembling is the opposite of Saul's fear: it is not the shaking of a man afraid of his enemies but the reverence of a man who has heard God speak. Eli trembled for the ark, Ezra's company trembled at the word. I hold that God looks for this trembling, and He says so Himself.
